# Program status: the research tech tree {#sec-program-status}

This appendix is the one place in the book that is a live status ledger rather than a presentation of settled knowledge: it records which experiments are running, planned, done or stopped, with dates, so that a reader can see what is still open. Every row links to the dated lab-notebook entry (@sec-notebook) holding the preregistration and verdict. Polished chapters cite results only once they are in the DONE state here.

## The tech tree {#sec-tech-tree}

The generalization campaign — the program's current phase — is run as an
explicit tech tree: every experiment is a node with a preregistered
question, a dependency, an acceptance criterion, and a dated verdict in
the lab notebook (@sec-notebook). Three architectures recur throughout.
**ISLA** is the program's product: an SE(3)-equivariant
slice-routing surrogate — exact under rotations and translations by
construction, with a measure-weighted similarity gauge (measure-weighted
centroid and RMS-radius reference length) as the reference configuration
for new runs since 2026-09-03; the checkpoints most of this book reports
predate that gauge and saw absolute scale through a constant reference
length (@sec-mt2-architecture). **GeoTransolver** is the strongest
external baseline, a soft-slice global-attention architecture with
pointwise raw-coordinate features and no equivariance contract.
**MeshTransformer (MT1)** is the original GLOBE-lineage architecture,
retained where its drive-linearity contract and exact kernel decoder make
it the exactness reference. The central open question the tree is
organized around is the **G2 transfer gap**: on the frozen
DrivAerML→SHIFT-SUV instrument, GeoTransolver's zero-shot error on a
held-out vehicle family improves with in-family training data (0.784 →
0.657 across five rungs, two seeds per rung, with per-seed reversals
inside the spread) while ISLA's stays flat — the one measured axis where
the baseline generalizes and the structured model does not.

This paragraph summarizes the ledger below as of 2026-09-07. Every
mechanism candidate for ISLA's cross-family transfer gap has been resolved
against (locality, absolute scale, measure completeness, label noise); the
similarity gauge fixed the density-robustness failure without moving
zero-shot transfer. The HiLift generalization ladder read out on both
halves: ISLA is 2.8x and 2.5x more accurate than GeoTransolver at 35 and 210
training cases and at parity at 1,260, and on the sealed regime-extrapolation
test both architectures degrade about 10x, ISLA with the lower absolute error
and GeoTransolver with the smaller ratio. The data-efficiency result has been
steel-manned from every side the program could construct: four GeoTransolver
controls (higher learning rate, doubled epochs, at both small rungs), a
same-family Transolver baseline (2.9x behind at 35, 1.3x at 210), a third
seed, and case-level paired statistics (180/180 cases at 35). Its mechanism
is not identified: five single-factor ablations of ISLA move the error by at
most 16%, and transplanting ISLA's drive-relative invariants into the
baselines gives Transolver 1.35x and GeoTransolver nothing. The
raw-coordinate discriminator on the stall split fell in its falsifier band
(d 12.7/13.3), so GeoTransolver's smaller extrapolation ratio is not carried
by its raw inputs. On the boundary→interior task GeoTransolver leads by
2.6x, latent volume tokens along anchor normals made ISLA worse, and the
exact-kernel line is closed on separated 3D aerodynamics. Still running: the
510-case rung, the 20,000-token floor test, the single-angle mechanism split,
and the 210-case third seed.

: The tech-tree ledger. Every status is as of 2026-09-07; evidence links go to the dated lab-notebook entry holding the preregistration and verdict. Rows whose verdicts were later voided, retracted, or overturned say so and link both the original and the correcting entry. {#tbl-tech-tree}


## Provenance {#sec-provenance}

Every quantitative claim in the polished chapters is computed live from a
checked-in artifact under `examples/cfd/mesh_transformer/results/` (JSON
reductions of evaluation runs, each named with the date of the run that
produced it), or is a literal quoted from one of those files with the file
named in the caption. The lab notebook (@sec-notebook) holds, for every
artifact, the preregistration that preceded the run, the launch record,
and the verdict entry; the tech-tree ledger above links each node to those
entries. Training runs, checkpoints and per-point predictions live on the
cluster in the task directory named in the notebook and are not needed to
regenerate any figure in this book.

Two protocol facts a reader should carry into every chapter: all HiLift and
DrivAerML training runs used the same frozen recipe (10,000 sampled surface
points per case, 500 epochs, bfloat16, no augmentation, two or more seeds),
and every sealed test split was evaluated exactly once under a configuration
committed before the first test case was read. Where a claim rests on a
two-seed comparison the text says so; where a paired per-case statistic
exists it is reported instead of, not in addition to, an adjective.
